thread:
maria: FYI started roll for rate_v2 at 14:03 UTC to 25% traffic in the canary slice.
aj: which tenants are in the canary? any immediate 5xx or auth issues?
maria: acme-inc reported spikes on /v1/generate and /v1/chat — seeing both 429s and p95 growth from ~180ms to ~3.1s. No auth errors in the traces.
support_bot: alert: tenant=acme-inc 429_increase=+410% window=5m p95=3100ms samples=52
kevin: paste a proxy sample and the quota counters for that tenant.
june: grabbing logs now. req=req_2026-03_ee7a1
maria: proxy line:
[14:06:12] req=req_2026-03_ee7a1 tenant=acme-inc route=/v1/generate rc=429 rule=rate_v2 bucket=10/10 wait=0 backend_latency=3120ms upstream=served
aj: bucket full (10/10) — that implies v2 dropped burst tokens from 20->10. Did we change any batching/prefix cache settings in policy v2?
maria: batching and cache unchanged. We intentionally decreased per-tenant burst_token budget to improve fairness, but forgot to adjust short client backoff behaviour and per-route timeouts. Immediate effect: aggressive 429s for bursty clients and queued requests piling up causing latency tail.
kevin: mitigation plan: 1) pause increasing traffic split, 2) restore previous burst_tokens for affected canary tenants, 3) monitor 429 and p95 for 15m. Who can patch burst_tokens?
june: I can. Command I'll run (targeting only canary tenants):
rbctl policy patch rate_v2 --set "burst_tokens=20" --selector canary=true
maria: Before executing, ensure the change is scoped (canary only) and add a shadow header so production tenants unaffected. Also open support ticket and send short customer note.
june: executing now. will post patch id.
support_bot: ticket created: SUP-4821 customer=acme-inc initial_note=sent_by_maria
june: patch applied at 14:08 UTC patch_id=patch-787
maria: sample after patch:
[14:09:02] req=req_2026-03_ee7a1 tenant=acme-inc route=/v1/generate rc=200 backend_latency=220ms
support_bot: metrics: tenant=acme-inc 429_rate -80% 3m p95_latency 220ms
aj: nice. Kevin, can you run a dashboard diff (pre/post) for 429 rate, p95, and auth errors and keep alert channel open for 30m?
kevin: on it. dashboards pinned. if any regression I'll abort the rollout and hold.
maria: Next steps: stop the cutover, add runbook items: "validate burst token impact under realistic client retry patterns" and "increase route backend timeout for /v1/generate to 5s during canaries". Also add a synthetic canary workload replay tool to catch tail latencies.
kevin: i'll own the runbook and the dashboard alert rule. assign aj to implement timeout change in canary config.
aj: will implement timeout bump and the staged ramp plan: 10% steps every 10m with observability gates.
maria: Support, send ACME short update: we rolled back the burst limit for your canary slice and performance restored; follow-up PM will share details and we’ll coordinate a safe re-rollout.
support_bot: ticket SUP-4821 updated status=customer_notified
maria: retro note: policy changes that shrink burst capacity need an explicit "backoff model check" in the canary checklist. Otherwise we risk antagonizing retrying clients.
kevin: agreed. logging action items and timeline. thanks everyone.
aj: thanks team :thumbsup:
